identity.name: Sorbitol (D-sorbitol; E420(i), with sorbitol syrup E420(ii))

function.mechanism: Polyol that provides sweetness and bulk, binds water as a humectant, and exerts osmotic effects at high intake.

adi.basis: No final EFSA ADI identified on reviewed EFSA pages; E420 re-evaluation is ongoing.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA sweeteners topic lists E420 as authorised with re-evaluation ongoing; 2023 EFSA call requested additional toxicological/genotoxicity data.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database for D-sorbitol (INS 420(i)) lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED.

concerns.summary: Mouse work (Cell, 2024) found prolonged sorbitol intolerance and diarrhea after antibiotic plus high-fat context due to reduced microbial sorbitol catabolism (Clostridia depletion).
A 2025 rat study reported dose-dependent nephrotoxicity biomarkers and histopathology after sub-chronic sorbitol exposure.
A zebrafish model study (Science Signaling, 2025) linked microbiome depletion and high sorbitol exposure to steatotic liver phenotypes, indicating a context-dependent metabolic risk signal.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA lists ADI as not specified for D-sorbitol (INS 420(i)).
Sorbitol is not listed as an IARC-classified agent in current IARC list data (update shown 2026-02-25).
FDA allows use under GRAS provisions in 21 CFR 184.1835 with GMP conditions.

adi_exceedance.notes: A numeric ADI exceedance calculation is not possible from reviewed data because JECFA ADI is 'not specified' and EFSA has no final published ADI while re-evaluation is ongoing.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators continue to permit sorbitol, with no IARC carcinogenic classification for sorbitol itself, but recent animal/mechanistic studies indicate dose- and context-dependent GI/metabolic concerns in susceptible settings.
key_factors: EU authorised and FDA GRAS status
EFSA re-evaluation ongoing with additional data requests
Emerging mechanistic and animal risk signals at high or specific exposure contexts
